pool.text: A particle of mass 3 kg is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of magnitude P N is applied to the particle, causing it to accelerate at a rate of 4 m/s\(^2\). Find the value of P.
pool.sol: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the net force acting on an object is equal to the product of its mass and acceleration, i.e., F = ma. In this case, the mass of the particle is m = 3 kg and its acceleration is a = 4 m/s\(^2\). The applied force P is the net force acting on the particle, as the surface is smooth and horizontal, meaning there are no other horizontal forces to consider. Therefore, P = ma = (3 kg) * (4 m/s\(^2\)) = 12 N. Thus, the value of P is 12 N. [M1][A1]

pool.text: A particle of mass \(m\) kg is placed on a rough inclined plane. The plane is inclined at an angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\). The particle is on the point of sliding down the plane. The coefficient of static friction between the particle and the plane is \(\mu_s\). Given that the acceleration due to gravity is \(g = 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2\), find the value of \(\mu_s\).
pool.sol: When a particle is on the point of sliding down an inclined plane, the angle of inclination \(\alpha\) is equal to the angle of friction \(\phi\), where \(\tan \phi = \mu_s\). \nGiven that \(\tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\), and the particle is on the point of sliding, we have \(\alpha = \phi\). \nTherefore, \(\mu_s = \tan \phi = \tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\). [M1][A1]
